correctness.rationale: An n-point Lip_0 polytope vertex is precisely a potential whose active tight-constraint graph is connected (incidence-normal rank n-1). Short pairs form a matching, so a connected graph requires a length-one tight edge, forcing range one. Each singleton then takes 0/1, and each matched pair must contain a 0 or 1 anchor and belong to exactly one of six feasible states; an interior mate must be short-tight to its anchor. The long tight edges form a connected bipartite anchor core whenever both polarities occur, proving the converse. Enumeration 6^k 2^(n-2k) - 2*3^k equals 3^k(2^(n-k)-2). Polar duality gives the facets. Exact integer-arithmetic spanning-tree enumeration matched all classifications in 36 bounded test cases (some duplicate k=0 metrics), used as corroboration, not universal proof. No assumptions beyond n>=3, disjoint pairs and 0<t_i<1 are needed.

value.rationale: The matched shortened edges constitute an intrinsically natural set of independent perturbations of the equilateral metric. The classification is complete across unbounded n, every matching size, and every independent continuous short length. The all-pairs equilateral facet number 2^n-2 changes to 3^k(2^(n-k)-2), yielding exponential asymptotic amplification for n=2k while remaining rigid under length variation. This exact polyhedral structural fact is not a routine primal-molecule deduction or a finite-table curiosity. Applications include sharp enumeration of dual Lipschitz potentials for tractable weighted metric geometries.
